title: Gidel bar Re’ulai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Gittin 34a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.34a.3-4) he sends a bill of divorce to his wife; he lived in the time of Abaye and Rava. There, [58b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.58b.10-11), he takes land from the district's residents on terms of paying its tax, and comes before Rav Papa. It is not known whether he was a Torah scholar.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ושם נח: means “and there, 58b,” not a man named Noah. The consulted passage names Giddul bar Re’ilai, tax arrangements and Rav Papa; Taska and Baga are not treated as two place names. The heading’s Re’ulai form remains.

The first passage gives the divorce and the ensuing disagreement between Abaye and Rava. The second names Giddul in a land-tax dispute that comes before Rav Pappa. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=860&lang=en) cites both and likewise leaves Giddul’s scholarly status open.
